title: Director of Procurement

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: With $207M in revenue, 10 locations across 16 states, and 20,000+ SKUs, the Director of Procurement manages supplier relationships, negotiates contracts, and optimizes the supply chain that keeps GSG's distribution network stocked. This role would care about Tedlar because: (1) Supplier reliability and product quality directly impact GSG's ability to serve sign manufacturers and graphics companies without backorders or quality complaints—Tedlar's 60+ years of proven performance and DuPont backing provides supply chain stability; (2) Total cost of ownership matters in distribution: While Tedlar may have premium positioning, its extreme durability (12-20+ years) means GSG's customers need fewer replacements, reducing GSG's inventory turnover costs and logistics expenses over time; (3) The recent Grimco acquisition (January 2025) likely triggered procurement consolidation initiatives—this is the exact window when new supplier relationships are evaluated and rationalized, making now the optimal time to introduce Tedlar as a strategic vendor; (4) Customer service metrics tied to this role improve when GSG stocks products that solve end-user pain points (UV damage, graffiti, premature failure)—Tedlar reduces complaint escalations and return processing. Their KPIs around supplier performance, inventory turns, and procurement cost savings align with adding a reliable, premium supplier that enhances customer satisfaction.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: This Director manages GSG's supplier portfolio across 20,000+ SKUs spanning 10 distribution locations in 16 states. They own vendor selection, contract negotiations, supply chain optimization, and likely report to a VP of Operations or CFO. With the Grimco acquisition closing in January 2025, they're currently in a procurement consolidation phase—evaluating which suppliers to retain, which to eliminate, and where gaps exist in the combined portfolio. They influence or directly approve new supplier relationships for product categories like protective films and overlaminates, and work closely with Product Management and Sales to ensure inventory meets customer demand without excess carrying costs.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: GSG's customers—sign manufacturers, large-format graphics companies, and vehicle wrap installers—need protective overlaminates for outdoor signage, architectural graphics, vehicle wraps, and transit applications. Tedlar directly addresses three procurement-relevant use cases: (1) Outdoor signage overlaminates where GSG's customers face warranty claims from UV degradation and cracking—Tedlar's 12-20+ year outdoor lifespan reduces defect returns flowing back through GSG's distribution channel; (2) Graffiti-resistant films for transit, architectural, and public signage applications where customers currently lack effective solutions—Tedlar's graffiti resistance (spray paint and markers wipe clean) fills a portfolio gap that GSG can monetize; (3) Premium vehicle wrap overlaminates where installers need reliable performance for fleet graphics lasting 7-10+ years—Tedlar's weather resistance (-70°F to 230°F) and fade resistance support GSG's premium customer segment.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This role owns KPIs including supplier on-time delivery rates, inventory turnover efficiency, procurement cost savings, and customer complaint resolution tied to product quality. They're measured on maintaining supply chain continuity across 10 locations while optimizing working capital. Adding Tedlar impacts their metrics positively: (1) DuPont's manufacturing reliability improves supplier performance scores and reduces stockout risk; (2) Tedlar's durability means GSG's customers order replacement films less frequently, which actually improves inventory turnover ratios by reducing dead stock of short-lifespan products that expire on shelves; (3) Fewer customer complaints about premature film failure reduce procurement's time spent managing returns, warranty claims, and expedited replacement shipments; (4) In the post-acquisition integration period, successfully adding a differentiated supplier like DuPont demonstrates strategic procurement value to new Grimco leadership.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Three timing factors make this the optimal outreach window: (1) The Grimco acquisition closed in January 2025—procurement teams are actively rationalizing supplier lists and identifying portfolio gaps right now, creating a 3-6 month window before supplier rosters freeze; (2) GSG is exhibiting at ISA Sign Expo 2025 (Booth #3325), which typically occurs in April—procurement needs to finalize new product additions 60-90 days before major trade shows to support sales team demos and promotional materials; (3) Spring 2025 represents the start of outdoor signage season when demand for protective films peaks, making this the natural procurement planning cycle for adding new overlaminate suppliers before summer installation activity.

personalization_hooks.hook: The Grimco acquisition just closed in January 2025, placing procurement in active supplier consolidation mode for the combined 10-location, 16-state distribution network
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead by acknowledging the integration challenge they're facing: 'I know GSG just completed the Grimco acquisition—as you're evaluating your supplier portfolio across the combined network, I wanted to introduce a protective film line that solves a specific gap your sign and graphics customers are asking about.' This positions you as helpful during a high-stakes transition period, not just another vendor adding to their workload.

personalization_hooks.hook: GSG actively promotes application tapes and overlaminates (RTape partnerships) but lacks a graffiti-resistant protective film option for transit, architectural, and public signage customers
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame Tedlar as a portfolio completion play: 'Your product line serves the graphics market well with RTape application solutions, but I'm seeing sign manufacturers and transit contractors asking distributors for graffiti-resistant overlaminates that can handle vandalism without replacement. Tedlar fills that gap—spray paint and permanent markers wipe clean without solvents.' This shows you understand their existing portfolio and how Tedlar complements rather than competes.

personalization_hooks.hook: As a $207M distributor managing 20,000+ SKUs, their procurement metrics reward suppliers who reduce customer complaint rates and return processing costs
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Connect Tedlar to their operational efficiency KPIs: 'One challenge I hear from distributors is the hidden cost of stocking short-lifespan films—customers call with premature failure complaints, returns eat into margins, and your team spends time expediting replacements. Tedlar's outdoor performance reduces those service calls because the film simply doesn't fail in 2-3 years like standard overlaminates. That operational benefit compounds across your 10 locations.' This speaks their language of total cost of ownership, not just product features.

recommended_approach: Lead with the acquisition timing and portfolio gap angle—acknowledge the Grimco integration reality upfront to show business awareness, then quickly pivot to how Tedlar solves a specific customer need (graffiti resistance) that their current supplier roster doesn't address. Keep the initial message focused on one concrete use case rather than overwhelming them with all of Tedlar's benefits. Close with a low-commitment ask: 'Would a 15-minute call make sense to explore whether this fits your procurement priorities post-acquisition?' This respects that they're busy with integration while positioning Tedlar as strategically relevant to their current decision-making window.
